speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many students currently benefit from the School Meals Programme; (b) whether equivalent financial assistance will be provided to students in lieu of the School Meals Programme subsidy if schools are closed or students are required to stay at home during the COVID-19 outbreak; and (c) whether the Ministry will study expanding the School Meals Programme to provide financial assistance for students during school holidays to avoid "holiday hunger".

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: asked the Minister for Education what plans have been made to ensure that all students, particularly those on the Ministry's Financial Assistance Scheme and Independent School Bursary Scheme, have the computer and broadband Internet resources to access online learning from their homes in the event of school closure or stay-at-home requirements due to the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As the School Meals Programme provides subsidies for meals purchased from the school canteen, the students will not be able to benefit from it if they are not in school.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When schools move to full home-based learning on 8 April 2020, this Wednesday, two things will happen for us to continue to assist them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: First, some of the students will continue to come to schools.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But today and tomorrow, schools will reach out to these students to see who would still need to come to school because they do not have support at home to do home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will register them and continue to let them come to school during this circuit breaker period.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is what we currently do for low-income households facing financial difficulty throughout the year, but the SSOs will do more to help needy families access financial assistance schemes rolled out as part of COVID-19 support measures.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I should also add that other than the SSOs, there are also other community partners such as the Community Development Councils (CDCs), donors who are coming forward to try to support these students, often through food vouchers for example, so that they continue to get their meals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The CDCs are studying this and once the details are worked out, they will announce the new measures.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On Assoc Prof Walter Theseira's second question on home-based learning and the availability of devices and Internet resources, let me first clarify that home-based learning is not solely done through online learning.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A substantial part of home-based learning is also in the form of readings or assignments to be done offline.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Schools will plan and implement a home-based learning programme that best suits the context of their curriculum and the profiles of their students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But the Member is rightfully concerned about the availability of devices and Internet access.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is an issue that MOE has been very preoccupied with, ever since we were planning home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you go to the community, to the households, many of them still encounter challenges.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, most students are reasonably equipped, but there will always be a minority that we must take care of as we move to home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One, for the students without computer and Internet access at home, schools will loan devices to these students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Today and tomorrow, we expect more students and parents to come forward, and we will loan them more if need be, so that everyone is properly equipped.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is why we are starting out home-based learning on Wednesday and not immediately.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is one day later than the companies, because we need to get this done properly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are also thankful to corporate sponsors who have stepped forward to provide free dongles and Internet subscriptions to many of these students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is no doubt – as the Member has pointed out or implied in his questions – that when schools move to home-based learning, students from the lower income group will be the most adversely affected.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And that is why we are moving to full home-based learning only now, and not earlier, because we know it creates a lot of disruption to people's lives.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Children from lower income families, from vulnerable families are most affected.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we are doing it now in support of the circuit breaker measures that will come into force this week.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is really part of our psychological unity – students, teachers, parents, all being part of it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And as the Speaker just said, we all rise to the call as one united people in tackling this crisis.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As it is, we are seeing long-term absenteeism starting to creep up in schools because of all the restrictions that have been implemented over the past weeks and due to the COVID-19 measures at schools as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But now that we have taken the decision to move to full home-based learning, let us now make the best out of the situation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MOE will mobilise the necessary resources to support this group of vulnerable students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I think we are all reassured that the Ministry is monitoring the situation closely, especially how to help low-income families and students transit to home-based learning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I understand it is not within his purview, necessarily, but I think it is important to have that assurance given by Government.
